title: Arbor Financial - Vendor Gating & Contract Playbook
topics: Vendor onboarding checklist and evidence pack
summary: Procurement and legal review focused on redlines to the MSA/DPA, clarifying SLA levels and remedies, and steps for getting pricing approved through Arbor's vendor gating. Actions include Redwood deliverables: updated redline, SOC2/ISO artifacts, and a tailored onboarding checklist.
action_items: Daniel Park: Upload redlined MSA + annotated DPA to shared folder; Due 2025-08-18
Priya Singh: Prepare technical evidence pack (SOC2 type II report excerpt, encryption architecture, KMS flow diagrams); Due 2025-08-20
Marcus Li: Share internal vendor-gating checklist and procurement timeline; Due 2025-08-15
Sofia Reyes: Provide specific DPA language requests (data subprocessor list, deletion SLA) as bullet points; Due 2025-08-19
next_steps: Redwood to send link to MSA redline + DPA stub
Customer to circulate redline to security and legal for one-week review
Schedule executive pricing approval call w/ CFO if procurement passes initial gating
Set up short technical checkpoint for bench testing (latency/cost) if procurement requests evidence
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-08-12
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Daniel Park (Redwood AE); Priya Singh (Redwood SE); Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Marcus Li (Arbor Procurement); Sofia Reyes (Arbor Legal); Ken Nakamura (Arbor Eng Lead); Aisha Taylor (Arbor Security)
Shared docs: Redwood MSA/DPA draft (link: drive.redwood/Arbor/MSA-DPA-2025), onboarding checklist (redwood.io/onboard/arbor)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
High-level: Walk through Redwood standard MSA and DPA; Arbor enumerated procurement gating requirements (PO, vendor risk assessment); agreement on Redwood providing SOC2 artifacts and KMS overview; pricing approval path requires final SOW and procurement PO.

[00:00] Daniel Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I see all the faces, I'll kick off quick. Um, we scheduled 50 minutes today to make sure we, uh, land on the gating steps so you can take this to procurement.

[00:18] Marcus Li: Thanks Daniel. High level - procurement needs clarity on the MSA redline and the DPA. We'll need to feed legal and security, and then there's an exec pricing sign-off if the numbers look good. Timeline is tight, we ideally want vendor approval by end of month.

[00:33] Daniel Park: Totally understood. Priya and I prepared a redline and we'll map each redline to policy reasons. Also we'll attach the SOC 2 material and an architecture diagram showing where customer data resides and KMS flow.

[00:50] Priya Singh: Quick note — on private deployments we can do a VPC control plane and customer-managed KMS, and on hosted we offer KMS integration with customer keys via KMS/HSM. There's a small doc in the pack that shows key custody.

[01:12] Sofia Reyes: When you say customer-managed KMS, do you mean full key ownership or wrapped keys? We need language about who is the key custodian for the DPA.

[01:25] Priya Singh: Good question. For the private model, you control the keys — you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) and we never persist the plain text in our control plane. For hosted, we support customer-managed keys in the cloud provider and we can integrate with your KMS via API. I'll send a diagram. Sorry if I said it fast, there was some lag.

[01:47] Ken Nakamura: Also, from an eng perspective, we want to understand the SLA for KV cache warmup and for tail-latency scenarios. If you give a 99.9 SLA what happens during maintenance windows? Do we get credits?

[02:05] Daniel Park: Our baseline SLA for the Dedicated plan is 99.95 for request success and a latency SLO we can include; credits are tiered — we proposed service credits in the MSA. We can quote specific numbers. Maintenance windows are announced and we provide automatic fallback to a regional pool when possible.

[02:30] Marcus Li: Procurement's checklist also asks for proof of compliance — SOC 2 type II attestation, penetration test summary, ISO 27001 cert if available. Do you have those docs?

[02:43] Lena Ortiz: Yes, we have a SOC 2 Type II report and a penetration test summary. We don't currently hold ISO 27001 but we have controls aligned; we can provide an attestation and evidence pack. We'll drop those into the shared folder.

[02:58] Aisha Taylor: For the DPA scope — Arbor requires data residency in the EU for EU customers and we need a subprocessor list with notification windows. Also deletion guarantees: when a customer requests deletion, what's the timeframe?

[03:18] Priya Singh: Deletion is handled by purge APIs; typical timeframe is 30 days for full purge from backups, but we can negotiate shorter windows for Dedicated or Private deployments. Subprocessor list is standard — we'll include our current infra partners and any managed services.

[03:35] Sofia Reyes: We also want the right to audit — can we include a clause for on-site or remote audit at least once a year?

[03:44] Daniel Park: We usually allow remote audits and provide logs and evidence; on-site audits for hosted are trickier but possible under enterprise agreements. For Private on-prem it's straightforward. We can add a clause with mutually agreed scope and cost allocation.

[03:59] Marcus Li: Pricing — procurement needs to know what triggers the executive review. Our finance requires a SOW and TCV above $150k to get CFO sign-off. Is that the band you typically see for Dedicated?

[04:15] Daniel Park: Yes that's typical. Dedicated commits usually start at the low six figures. We'll prepare a SOW draft tied to the Dedicated pool sizing and expected tokens/month. If the TCV is above your threshold we'll schedule the CFO call — Priya, can you provide an estimate for a 2x redundancy pool?

[04:33] Priya Singh: Yeah, give me your expected throughput and target latency, I'll model two configs and include cost delta for quantized vs full precision. Also we'll show the expected cost per 1M tokens with caching assumptions.

[04:50] Ken Nakamura: One more tech ask — what's the data retention default for logs and audit trails? We need 1 year for audit logs and at least 30 days for request payload storage.

[05:02] Lena Ortiz: Our default is 90 days for request payloads, audit logs 1 year. We can extend retention for an add-on. We'll note that in the onboarding checklist.

[05:18] Sofia Reyes: On indemnity and limitation of liability — we need to tighten the cap for regulated data to be more than just a multiple of fees. Can we discuss carve-outs for gross negligence?

[05:31] Daniel Park: Standard carve-outs for gross negligence and wilful misconduct are included; we can discuss adjusting caps for regulated workloads under the Private deployment. I'll flag that for legal to review redline.

[05:48] Marcus Li: Procurement also requires procurement evidence: a UC/TO report, vendor risk scorecard, and a named SLA clause to insert into our vendor management system. Can Redwood provide a one-page SLA summary that we can paste into our tool?

[06:05] Daniel Park: Absolutely. We'll produce a one-page SLA summary and a vendor evidence packet. We'll also provide a short 'how we handle data' one-pager for your risk team.

[06:20] Aisha Taylor: Encryption at rest and in transit — please confirm TLS 1.2+ and AES-256 at rest, plus key lifecycle details. Also are there any subprocessors in APAC that host data?

[06:35] Priya Singh: TLS 1.2+ yes; we recommend 1.3 when possible. AES-256 for at-rest. Key lifecycle: rotation, revocation, backup — we'll include the diagram. Subprocessors vary by region; we'll give you the list and note which ones host EU data.

[06:53] Sofia Reyes: For the DPA, can you accept a 30-day deletion SLA and a 15-day notification for subprocessor changes? That's what Arbor's privacy policy requires.

[07:08] Daniel Park: We can probably accept 30-day deletion for Dedicated and Private; for hosted we typically do 30 days but need to confirm backups language. Subprocessor change notifications we typically do 30 days, but 15 days is possible for enterprise agreements — we'll flag as a redline.

[07:25] Marcus Li: Ok, good. Walk me through the approval path: after you send redline, legal will propose changes, procurement will score vendor risk, then finance will sign off on pricing. How long should we expect?

[07:40] Daniel Park: If everyone moves fast, 2–3 weeks is feasible: we send redline day 1, your legal returns comments in 3–5 business days, procurement does vendor gating in parallel, finance needs the SOW and TCV for formal approval — that's typical. We'll put milestones in the shared folder.

[07:57] Ken Nakamura: One technical clarification — if we go dedicated, will there be dedicated ingress endpoints in our VPC? We need private connectivity and explicit egress rules.

[08:12] Priya Singh: Yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on cloud. We can provide an engineering runbook for network setup. That's in the onboarding checklist.

[08:27] Lena Ortiz: Quick note — earlier you asked for a penetration test summary; we have a redacted summary we can share. Also our SOC2 report will be redacted for customer-specific info, usual practice.

[08:42] Sofia Reyes: For indemnification again — who is the party responsible for model outputs that cause regulatory risk? We need to make sure liability around model hallucinations is addressed.

[08:58] Daniel Park: Liability for outputs is a complicated area; we typically disclaim certain downstream harms and provide best-effort controls (content filters, allow-lists). For regulated use cases, Private deployment or stricter SLOs are recommended and can change contractual allocation. We'll be explicit in the DPA/MSA redline.

[09:17] Marcus Li: Great. Can we also get a sample PO template and a sample SOW? Procurement needs that to fast-track purchase orders.

[09:26] Daniel Park: Yes, we'll include a PO template and a SOW draft tied to pool size and expected token commitments.

[09:35] Aisha Taylor: One last question from security: do you provide access logs per token or per request? We need individual request IDs mapped to customer IDs.

[09:45] Priya Singh: We emit request-level logs with request IDs and metadata, and those are exportable to your SIEM. Token-level logs are more sensitive but we provide token counts and usage metrics.

[09:59] Sofia Reyes: Ok, thank you. On the DPA delete clause please include obligation to confirm deletion in writing once complete — that's standard for us.

[10:10] Daniel Park: We can include written confirmation for deletions and offer a deletion attestation. We'll add that to the DPA redline.

[10:20] Marcus Li: Anything else from Redwood side?

[10:25] Daniel Park: Quick administrative items — we'll send the redline, the evidence pack, the SLA one-pager, and the SOW. Expect those in the shared folder by Monday EOD.

[10:34] Marcus Li: Sounds good. If procurement gates you, we'll send a vendor risk scorecard and then loop in finance.

[10:40] Sofia Reyes: We might ask for one or two small redlines around indemnity; we'll log them and get back.

[10:48] Daniel Park: Understood. Priya, Lena — any closing technical items?

[10:53] Priya Singh: I'll prepare the KMS flow diagram and the onboarding runbook for VPC peering; I'll also include cost estimates for quantized models.

[11:02] Lena Ortiz: I'll package SOC2, pentest summary, and the onboarding checklist into a single evidence zip for Marcus.

[11:09] Marcus Li: Perfect. Let's do a follow-up 30-minute check-in next Tuesday to go over redline comments. I'll send the calendar invite after today's call.

[11:20] Daniel Park: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts. Meeting adjourned.

End-of-transcript notes: Observed a couple of dropped words in the recording, some overlap at 06:20–06:35, and a brief audio glitch around 01:25 which caused Priya's KMS explanation to be partially garbled.
